gotcha.title: A client that isn't `mut`
gotcha.looks_fine: A client feels like a read-only handle you make calls through, so declaring it mutable seems odd.
gotcha.rust_sees: The generated `say_hello` takes `&mut self` (you can read the signature in the `generated` session above). Calling a `&mut self` method needs a `mut` variable.
gotcha.why: It is the rule from [Mutable borrows](/learn/mutable-borrows/): a `&mut` borrow needs a variable declared `mut`. tonic's [`Channel` docs](https://docs.rs/tonic/0.14.6/tonic/transport/struct.Channel.html) explain the same requirement one level down, on the `Channel` that the generated client wraps: sending a request "requires a `&mut self` and thus can only send one request in flight", which they call "intentional" and required by the `Service` contract of the tower library. Need several tasks to make calls at once? The same docs say cloning a `Channel` is "cheap and encouraged", because the connection runs in a background task that the clones talk to. The docs say that about a `Channel`; this page does not run a program that clones the generated client.
